# Readiness Probes: Checklist and Antipatterns

> Why the mission-capability / dependency split matters (Kubernetes Service
> endpoint dropping, ServiceMonitor scrape gaps) lives in
> [knowledgebase/observability/readiness-probes.md](https://github.com/jewzaam/knowledgebase/blob/main/observability/readiness-probes.md).

## Concrete checklist

For a new long-lived service that exposes both a readiness probe and
`/metrics`:

1. **List startup prerequisites.** What does the process require BEFORE
   it can serve a request meaningfully? (Credentials present, config
   parseable, output path writable.) These — and only these — gate
   `/readyz`.
2. **List runtime dependencies.** What can fail at request time without
   stopping the process? (Upstream API, token refresh, cache, downstream
   writes.) These get metrics, not probe failures.
3. **Wire `/readyz` to a one-time startup check** OR a re-evaluable
   check that ONLY inspects prerequisite state. Do not bind it to "last
   upstream call succeeded".
4. **Add gauges for every runtime dependency.** Boolean or
   monotonic-counter form. HELP text spells out the semantics.
5. **Write PromQL alerts against the metrics**, not against
   `kube_pod_status_ready`. The Pod ready signal alerts on misconfig;
   the metric alerts on dependency sadness.

## Antipatterns

- **`/readyz` gates on "last upstream call succeeded".** Initial cold start
  of a freshly deployed Pod stays NotReady until the first successful
  upstream call, hiding credential failures behind a probe flap. Once the
  dependency starts flapping, the Pod cycles in and out of the Service, and
  `ServiceMonitor` scrapes go missing during the exact window the operator
  is trying to debug.
- **`/readyz` gates on cache freshness.** Same failure mode: cache age is
  dependency state, not capability state. The Pod is still capable of
  serving cached data or returning a stale-flag.
- **`/healthz` (liveness) gates on dependency health.** Pod restart loop.
  The new Pod hits the same sad dependency and fails the same way. Wastes
  operator time looking at restart counts that aren't the real symptom.
